cell_type_model: HeLa cells expressing IL20RB and IL22RA1; epithelial receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: Recombinant IL-24 stimulation of IL20RB/IL22RA1-expressing cells; pSTAT3 immunoblot and receptor-complex signaling assays
relation_type: IL-24 engages the IL20RB-IL22RA1 heteromeric receptor complex and activates JAK/STAT signaling
pathway_branch: IL24-IL20RB/IL22RA1-JAK1/TYK2-STAT3 epithelial signaling branch
limitations: The photocaged-IL-24 study validates pSTAT3 in engineered HeLa cells; receptor-complex stoichiometry and cell-type-specific outputs outside epithelial systems remain context dependent.

cell_type_model: Recombinant receptor-complex systems; primary and naive CD4 T cells; mouse cardiomyocytes and pressure-overload models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-33/ST2 binding and structural complex assembly; ST2 or MyD88 deficiency; IL-33 stimulation; NF-kB/MAPK, cytokine, hypertrophy, and in vivo cardiac assays
relation_type: IL-33 activates the ST2/IL1RAcP receptor complex and recruits the MyD88-dependent IL-1-family relay
pathway_branch: IL33-IL1RL1/ST2-IL1RAP-MyD88-IRAK4-TRAF6-NF-kB/MAPK inflammatory and cardioprotective branch
limitations: The structural paper establishes the ternary receptor complex, while functional studies use ST2L and MyD88 perturbations; NF-kB/MAPK outputs are not a single terminal-TF assignment.

cell_type_model: CSF-1R-deficient U251 human glioblastoma cells; mouse brain and macrophage/arthritis models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-34 affinity chromatography and cell binding; PTPRZ1 depletion or chondroitinase treatment; recombinant IL-34; FAK/paxillin phosphorylation, proliferation, motility, and genetic arthritis assays
relation_type: Direct IL-34 binding to PTPRZ1/PTP-zeta with PTPRZ1-dependent receptor-proximal phosphorylation and cellular effects
pathway_branch: IL34-PTPRZ1 chondroitin-sulfate-dependent receptor branch to FAK/paxillin and myeloid/neural-cell outputs
limitations: PTPRZ1 glycosaminoglycan modification is required for binding; the strongest molecular work is in glioblastoma and the disease study is macrophage focused, so the relay is not a universal substitute for CSF1R signaling.

cell_type_model: Mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages with Il13ra1 or Il4ra deletion; human fibroblast and airway smooth-muscle comparator cultures
assay_or_perturbation: IL-4 stimulation with receptor-chain knockout or neutralization; STAT6 DNA-binding/phosphorylation and alternative macrophage activation readouts
relation_type: IL-4 signals through the type-II IL-4 receptor composed of IL4RA and IL13RA1, with STAT6 activation and cell-state outputs
pathway_branch: IL4-IL4RA/IL13RA1-JAK1/JAK3-STAT6 alternative-activation and allergic-response branch
limitations: IL4 can also signal through the type-I IL4RA-IL2RG complex; the type-II assignment here is supported by receptor-chain genetics and should not be merged with that branch.

cell_type_model: Mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages and lymphoid/allergic disease models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-4 stimulation with Il2rg or Il4ra deficiency; STAT6 activation, gene-expression, and receptor-dependent immune-function assays
relation_type: IL-4 activates the type-I IL4RA-IL2RG receptor complex and the JAK/STAT6 relay
pathway_branch: IL4-IL4RA/IL2RG-JAK1/JAK3-STAT6 lymphoid and type-II immune-response branch
limitations: Residual IL-4-induced STAT6 in Il2rg-deficient macrophages can arise through type-II receptors containing IL13RA1; receptor composition is cell-state dependent.

cell_type_model: IL-5-responsive TF-1 and YY-1 cells; peripheral eosinophils; recombinant IL-5 receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: IL-5 stimulation; receptor-mutant and transfected-cell assays; JAK2 and STAT5 phosphorylation/DNA-binding; receptor structural and photo-cross-linking studies
relation_type: IL-5 engages the IL5RA-CSF2RB/beta-c receptor complex and activates JAK2/STAT5 with eosinophil growth and activation outputs
pathway_branch: IL5-IL5RA/CSF2RB-JAK2-STAT5 eosinophil proliferation and activation branch
limitations: The receptor alpha/beta-c structural work and signaling studies use recombinant or hematopoietic models; STAT1 is also observed in eosinophils, but STAT5 is the reproducible endpoint.

cell_type_model: M1 myeloid cells with engineered gp130; primary human lung fibroblasts; mouse and human progenitor/granulocyte models
assay_or_perturbation: IL-6 stimulation; gp130 mutation and deficiency; receptor binding; JAK/STAT phosphorylation; STAT3/STAT1 DNA-binding and differentiation/response assays
relation_type: IL-6 assembles the IL6RA-IL6ST/gp130 receptor complex and activates the gp130 JAK/STAT relay
pathway_branch: IL6-IL6RA/IL6ST-JAK1/JAK2/TYK2-STAT3/STAT1 acute-phase, inflammatory, and differentiation branch
limitations: IL-6 responsiveness requires gp130 expression and varies by cell type; STAT3 is the principal endpoint, while STAT1 can also be recruited through distinct gp130 phosphotyrosine modules.

cell_type_model: Mouse lymphoid development and Stat5-deficient models; human and murine lymphoid cells
assay_or_perturbation: IL-7 stimulation; IL7R/IL2RG/JAK perturbation and Stat5 genetic deficiency; receptor phosphorylation, STAT5 activation, survival and lymphoid-development assays
relation_type: IL-7 activates the IL7R-IL2RG common-gamma receptor complex and the JAK1/JAK3-STAT5 relay
pathway_branch: IL7-IL7R/IL2RG-JAK1/JAK3-STAT5-PI3K/AKT lymphoid survival and development branch
limitations: The receptor pathway is well established, but the cited genetic study spans developmental and lymphoid contexts; STAT1/STAT3 can be minor context-dependent outputs.

cell_type_model: IL-9-responsive T-cell lines and engineered receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: IL-9 stimulation; receptor heteromerization and cytoplasmic tyrosine-mutant assays; JAK1/JAK3 and STAT1/STAT3/STAT5 activation; apoptosis/proliferation assays
relation_type: IL-9 activates the IL9R-IL2RG receptor complex and recruits JAK1/JAK3 to activate multiple STAT factors
pathway_branch: IL9-IL9R/IL2RG-JAK1/JAK3-STAT1/STAT3/STAT5 T-cell survival and proliferation branch
limitations: The primary study used a T-cell line and reports several STAT complexes; the relative contribution of STAT1, STAT3, and STAT5 varies with receptor and cellular context.

cell_type_model: Human endothelial and leukemic-cell receptor-complex systems; human prostate cancer cells
assay_or_perturbation: Activin-A affinity labeling/co-precipitation with endoglin and ligand-binding kinase receptors; endoglin, ACVR2A/BMPRII, and ALK2 perturbation with Smad1 and invasion assays
relation_type: Activin A/INHBA associates with ENG as an accessory component of a signaling receptor complex, but ENG does not bind activin independently of a ligand-binding kinase receptor
pathway_branch: Activin-A-ACVR2A/ACVR2B-ALK2/ALK4-ENG receptor-complex accessory branch
limitations: The primary study requires coexpression of an activin ligand-binding kinase receptor and does not establish ENG as a standalone signaling receptor for INHBA; downstream Smad1 evidence belongs to the assembled activin/endoglin complex.

cell_type_model: Human multiple-myeloma cells; mouse and human preadipocyte/adipocyte receptor knockout and reconstitution systems
assay_or_perturbation: Insulin stimulation; IGF1R/INSR hybrid-receptor immunoprecipitation; receptor and IRS phosphorylation; receptor knockout/reconstitution; gene-expression and proliferation assays
relation_type: Insulin can activate IGF1R-containing hybrid receptors and propagate IRS/PI3K-AKT and MAPK signals
pathway_branch: Ins2-IGF1R/INSR-hybrid receptor-IRS1/2-PI3K-AKT and RAS-ERK growth/metabolic branch
limitations: Insulin has highest canonical affinity for INSR; the IGF1R edge is strongest in hybrid-receptor or high-IGF1R contexts and is not equivalent to canonical INSR signaling.

cell_type_model: Primary human/rodent adipocytes and receptor knockout/reconstitution preadipocytes
assay_or_perturbation: Insulin stimulation; insulin-receptor and IRS tyrosine-phosphorylation assays; PI3K inhibition; receptor knockout/reconstitution and gene-expression measurements
relation_type: Insulin activates the INSR tyrosine-kinase receptor and recruits IRS scaffolds to PI3K-AKT and RAS-ERK pathways
pathway_branch: Ins2-INSR-IRS1/2-PI3K-AKT-mTOR and RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK metabolic, survival, and gene-regulatory branch
limitations: The studies emphasize receptor and IRS signaling rather than a single terminal TF; output amplitude depends on INSR/IGF1R abundance and adipocyte differentiation state.

cell_type_model: HEK293 cells stably expressing human or rat RXFP2; receptor-mutant and binding systems
assay_or_perturbation: INSL3 saturation/competition binding; RXFP2 mutagenesis; cAMP dose-response and receptor activation assays
relation_type: Direct INSL3 binding and productive activation of the RXFP2 GPCR
pathway_branch: INSL3-RXFP2-Gs/adenylyl-cyclase-cAMP receptor activation and reproductive/endocrine output branch
limitations: RXFP2 activation can be modulated by receptor dimerization and ligand-specific activation modes; the cited studies do not establish a terminal TF.

cell_type_model: HEK293 cells expressing RXFP3/RXFP4 and relaxin-family receptor chimeras
assay_or_perturbation: INSL5 binding, receptor chimeras, and functional GPCR pharmacology comparing native RXFP3 and RXFP4
relation_type: Low-affinity INSL5-RXFP3 interaction is reported as an antagonist/boundary, not a productive INSL5 receptor relay
pathway_branch: INSL5-RXFP4 productive signaling versus RXFP3 low-affinity receptor-specificity boundary
limitations: INSL5 is selective for RXFP4; native RXFP3 shows weak or antagonistic interaction and no validated INSL5-triggered downstream relay was retained.

cell_type_model: CHO-RXFP4 cells; human NCI-H716 enteroendocrine cells; MIN6 mouse insulinoma cells
assay_or_perturbation: INSL5 stimulation; AlphaScreen and BRET G-protein/arrestin assays; pertussis-toxin and G-protein rescue; cAMP, ERK1/2, Akt, p38, Ca2+, insulin secretion and proliferation assays
relation_type: Direct INSL5-RXFP4 activation recruits Gi/o and produces receptor-proximal and cellular signaling outputs
pathway_branch: INSL5-RXFP4-Gi/o-cAMP inhibition-Src/PI3K/MEK-ERK/Akt/p38/S6RP gut endocrine branch
limitations: The strongest pathway dissection is in engineered CHO-RXFP4 cells; some proposed intermediary links are inhibitor-based and the study did not identify a terminal TF.

cell_type_model: Primary human CD4 T cells; CD46-transgenic mouse erythrocytes; recombinant CD46 and Jag1 proteins
assay_or_perturbation: ELISA and surface-plasmon-resonance binding; CD3/CD46 stimulation; Jag1 and Notch perturbation; HES1/RBPJ and cytokine transcript assays
relation_type: Direct JAG1-CD46 ligand binding with CD46-dependent Notch receptor-complex crosstalk and immune functional output
pathway_branch: JAG1-CD46-Notch1/2-HES1/RBPJ crosstalk controlling IFN-gamma to IL-10 T-cell switching
limitations: The study establishes direct binding and Notch crosstalk but does not resolve a kinase relay or direct TF occupancy; HES1/RBPJ transcript changes are retained as pathway/function evidence, not a terminal-TF assignment.

cell_type_model: CHO-KISS1R cells and GT1-7 hypothalamic neuronal cells
assay_or_perturbation: Kisspeptin stimulation; intracellular calcium imaging; receptor internalization/recycling perturbation with dynasore, brefeldin A, and phenylarsine oxide
relation_type: KISS1 activates the KISS1R GPCR and produces sustained receptor-dependent calcium signaling
pathway_branch: KISS1-KISS1R-Gq/11-PLCbeta-IP3/DAG-Ca2+-PKC-ERK reproductive-neuroendocrine branch
limitations: The cited primary study emphasizes Ca2+ signaling and receptor trafficking; Gq/PLC and ERK pathway placement is consistent with receptor pharmacology but no terminal TF was directly measured.

cell_type_model: HSC-like hematopoietic progenitor lines; primary human erythroid progenitors; primary CML CD34-positive progenitors
assay_or_perturbation: Stem-cell-factor stimulation; KIT phosphorylation; PI3K, Raf/MEK/ERK, and Akt inhibition; progenitor survival and colony assays
relation_type: SCF/KIT ligand-receptor activation drives receptor-proximal tyrosine-kinase signaling and hematopoietic cellular outputs
pathway_branch: KITL-KIT-SRC/PI3K-AKT and RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK hematopoietic survival, proliferation, and differentiation branch
limitations: KIT signaling is lineage and differentiation-state dependent; PI3K dependence of ERK differs between immature progenitors and more mature mast-cell/erythroid contexts, and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: L1-CAM/EGFR transfected cells and neuronal adhesion models
assay_or_perturbation: L1-mediated homophilic interaction; EGFR kinase assays, receptor association, phosphorylation, and neurite/adhesion perturbation
relation_type: L1CAM-dependent EGFR association/transactivation is a receptor-complex relay rather than an isolated direct ligand-binding claim
pathway_branch: L1CAM-EGFR-cis/trans interaction-RTK phosphorylation-MAPK/neurite-adhesion branch
limitations: The primary study indicates that trans L1-EGFR interaction alone is insufficient and that cis co-organization is required for kinase activation; direct L1CAM-to-EGFR ligand activity should not be generalized beyond this complex context.

cell_type_model: Recombinant human L1 Ig-like domain; endothelial and platelet integrin adhesion systems; neural/cell-adhesion comparator models
assay_or_perturbation: Purified-domain integrin binding, RGD competition, divalent-cation dependence, and integrin-mediated cell attachment assays
relation_type: Direct RGD-dependent L1CAM binding to the alpha5beta1 integrin complex
pathway_branch: L1CAM-alpha5beta1 adhesion and focal-adhesion signaling boundary
limitations: The primary binding study establishes the extracellular interaction and adhesion but does not isolate a unique L1CAM-alpha5beta1 intracellular cascade; generic integrin FAK/Src outputs were not promoted to a direct L1CAM-specific relay.

cell_type_model: Recombinant human L1 Ig-like domain; endothelial and platelet integrin adhesion systems
assay_or_perturbation: Purified-domain integrin binding, RGD competition, divalent-cation dependence, and integrin-mediated cell attachment assays
relation_type: Direct RGD-dependent L1CAM binding to the alphaVbeta3 integrin complex
pathway_branch: L1CAM-alphaVbeta3 adhesion and integrin outside-in signaling boundary
limitations: The direct interaction is established, but the cited exact-pair work does not provide a uniquely assigned L1CAM-alphaVbeta3 kinase-to-TF relay; integrin-family pathway evidence was not transferred.

cell_type_model: Purified laminin-1 or alpha1-chain fragments; recombinant/purified alpha1beta1 integrin and laminin-adhesion cell systems
assay_or_perturbation: Solid-phase binding, surface-plasmon-resonance, integrin-specific antibody inhibition, and cell-attachment assays
relation_type: Laminin-alpha1-containing material binds the alpha1beta1 integrin complex; this row retains the alpha1 chain/alpha1-subunit component relationship
pathway_branch: LAMA1-alpha1beta1 extracellular matrix adhesion branch
limitations: The strongest assays use intact laminin-1 or alpha1-chain fragments and the assembled alpha1beta1 receptor; no isolated alpha1-subunit intracellular relay or terminal TF was demonstrated.

cell_type_model: Purified laminin-2 alpha2-chain short-arm domains; myoblast, neural, and laminin-adhesion systems
assay_or_perturbation: Integrin-specific antibody inhibition, recombinant alpha2-chain domain adhesion, and neurite-outgrowth assays
relation_type: Laminin-alpha2 domain VI directly supports alpha1beta1-mediated cell adhesion
pathway_branch: LAMA2-alpha1beta1 laminin adhesion and peripheral-nerve/muscle matrix branch
limitations: The direct interaction is mapped to laminin-alpha2 domain VI and the assembled alpha1beta1 receptor; downstream kinase signaling was not resolved for this exact pair.

cell_type_model: Human erythrocyte Lutheran/BCAM ectodomain and recombinant laminin-511/521 systems
assay_or_perturbation: X-ray crystallography, small-angle X-ray scattering, site-directed mutagenesis, and recombinant ligand-binding assays
relation_type: Direct laminin-alpha5/laminin-511-521 binding to the BCAM/Lutheran extracellular receptor
pathway_branch: LAMA5-BCAM/Lutheran extracellular matrix adhesion and vaso-occlusive boundary
limitations: BCAM/Lutheran is an adhesion receptor with a short cytoplasmic tail; the structural binding studies do not establish a defined intracellular kinase relay or terminal TF.

cell_type_model: Cultured hypothalamic and peripheral cells; mouse leptin-receptor signaling and physiology models
assay_or_perturbation: Leptin stimulation; long-form LEPR mutagenesis at Tyr985/Tyr1138; JAK2, SHP2/ERK, STAT3, SOCS3, and physiological-response assays
relation_type: Leptin activates the long LEPR isoform and its JAK2-linked intracellular relay
pathway_branch: LEP-LEPR-JAK2-SHP2/ERK and Tyr1138-STAT3-SOCS3 metabolic and neuroendocrine branch
limitations: Only the long LEPR isoform is a robust signaling receptor; receptor isoform, hypothalamic cell state, and leptin sensitivity determine the relative contribution of STAT3 and ERK branches.
